official.deadline_central_display: 19 March 2027 (latest scholarship deadline in the AY2027 round; most international qualifications close 20 January 2027)
official.deadline_note: The scholarship application period is the same as the admission application period, so the deadline depends on qualification: 20 January 2027 (NUS High School Diploma and most international qualifications), 21 February 2027 (Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore), 19 March 2027 (Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level and IB Diploma). Document deadlines are separate and later: photograph and referee appraisal by 26 March 2027 (GCE 'A' level and IB), 28 February 2027 (polytechnic diploma), 27 January 2027 (NUS High School Diploma). The official page states that applications submitted after the closing date will not be considered.
official.application_cycle: AY2027/2028 admission round (application windows October 2026 - March 2027)
official.status_note: For the AY2027 round NTU's important-dates page publishes windows opening 15 October 2026 (IB Diploma and most international qualifications) and 1 December 2026 (NUS High School Diploma), with the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level window opening on the day of A-level results release and the polytechnic diploma window opening 1 February 2027. As at 10 October 2026 the NTU admission portals still show applications as closed for the current cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant).

Living allowance of S$6,500 per academic year
Accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year (applicable to scholarship holders who reside in NTU hostels only)
Travel grant of up to S$8,000 for an overseas programme subject to terms and conditions in the Travel Grant Form (for new cohorts from AY2025)
Enrolment into NTU's flagship undergraduate college - NTU Honours College
eligibility: Successful awardees should read a full-time undergraduate degree programme; the scholarship will cover the years of study at NTU

Possess outstanding academic achievements in the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications
requirements: Submit your application for admission before submitting your application for scholarship
Must not, without the approval of the University, hold concurrently any other scholarships, bursaries, university loans or awards
Maintain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.5 over 5.0, with academic performance reviewed every semester
Take on the role of student ambassador, or any other similar role representing the university (publicity talks, receiving guests), as and when called upon

documents: Scholarship application form, accessed by logging in with the NTU application number
Personal essay of not more than 250 words answering the 1 compulsory topic included in the form
Online referee's appraisal completed by a school teacher who is not a family member or relative, submitted within 7 days of the scholarship application

Scholarship selection interviews take place between March and May; only shortlisted applicants are informed via e-mail by mid-May, and applicants offered the Medicine or Renaissance Engineering Programme must check with the school for the outcome
coverage: Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant)
Living allowance of S$6,500 per academic year
Accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year, applicable to scholarship holders who reside in NTU hostels only
Travel grant of up to S$8,000 for an overseas programme, subject to the terms and conditions in the Travel Grant Form, for new cohorts from AY2025
Enrolment into NTU's flagship undergraduate college, NTU Honours College
application_method: Submit the NTU application for admission first; you need the assigned NTU application number

Open the scholarship application form via the 'Apply for Scholarship' link at the end of your online admission application, or via the reserved-programme login, and log in with your application number
Applicants with Year 12 equivalent results apply through the separate international applicant scholarship login before the application closing date for that qualification
Complete the personal essay (not more than 250 words, 1 compulsory topic) and upload a recent passport-size photo (digital image)

official.application_route: Apply for NTU undergraduate admission first, then submit the scholarship form through the 'Apply for Scholarship' link (or the separate international login for Year 12 equivalent results) using your NTU application number
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate degree programme at NTU
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all nationalities; no bond is attached to the Nanyang Global Scholarship apart from the three-year bond applicable to all Singapore PRs and international students under the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme
official.international_eligibility: Open to all nationalities. Applicants with Year 12 equivalent qualifications apply through a separate scholarship login and attend selection interviews within 2 months of the NTU programme offer; other international qualification windows close 20 January 2027 or 19 March 2027 depending on the qualification
official.duration: The scholarship covers up to the normal programme duration on condition that the scholarship holder maintains a record of good academic performance and exemplary conduct
official.description: The Nanyang Global Scholarship is awarded to outstanding freshmen pursuing undergraduate programmes and recognises students with outstanding academic results, strong leadership abilities and very good co-curricular records. It provides full coverage of subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant plus living, accommodation, travel and computer allowances, and enrols awardees into NTU's flagship undergraduate college, the NTU Honours College.
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page itself publishes no English requirement. NTU's undergraduate admissions require an accepted English-language proficiency test for applicants who hold or are sitting selected qualifications (PRC Gao Kao, Taiwan GSAT, South Korean CSAT/High School Diploma, HKDSE, Vietnam High School Graduation Certificate, Thai Mathayom 6, Indonesian Ijazah SMA, or applicants who did not take English language in Junior and Senior High School or took it only as a second language): IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (Writing 6.5, Speaking 6.5), TOEFL 90, PTE Academic 55, C1 Advanced 170, SAT 1250, ACT composite 30 or AST English 220, with scores valid 2 years (SAT/ACT 5 years).

not_confirmed: A scholarship-specific English requirement (none is published on the scholarship page; the figures recorded are NTU's general undergraduate admission requirements)
Number of awards offered per cycle (not published)
verification.notes: All amounts (S$6,500 living allowance, S$2,000 accommodation allowance, S$8,000 travel grant, S$2,000 computer allowance), the tuition-fee wording, terms, application steps and selection timeline were read directly off NTU's Nanyang Global Scholarship page; per-qualification deadlines were cross-checked on NTU's Important dates page; the English figures come from NTU's General Admission Requirements page.

applicant_utility.summary: NTU's flagship freshman award wipes out the subsidised tuition bill and layers on S$6,500 a year for living costs, a hostel allowance, an overseas-programme travel grant and a computer allowance, so an awardee needs very little family support. Everything rides on the admission application: the scholarship form only unlocks once you hold an NTU application number, and a teacher's appraisal must land within 7 days of your submission. Interviews run between March and May, and only shortlisted applicants hear anything, by e-mail, around mid-May.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top school-leavers of any nationality - GCE 'A' level, Singapore polytechnic diploma, NUS High School, IB or Year 12 equivalent - with outstanding results, a strong co-curricular record and demonstrated leadership who can hold a CGPA of 3.5 and take on ambassador duties.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the NTU admission application first; the scholarship form is only reachable once you have your NTU application number
Confirm your qualification's closing date early: 20 January 2027 for most international qualifications, 21 February 2027 for Singapore polytechnic diplomas, 19 March 2027 for GCE 'A' level and IB
Pre-arrange a school teacher referee (not a relative) and warn them the online appraisal is due within 7 days of your scholarship submission
Draft the 250-word essay on the single compulsory topic and have a digital passport-size photo ready before the portal opens
Diarise the separate photo and appraisal deadlines, which fall about a week after the scholarship closing date
Keep e-mail accessible from March onward; shortlisted candidates are contacted directly and may be called at short notice
common_rejection_risks: Referee appraisal missing the 7-day window - only one appraisal may be submitted online, so there is no second chance with another teacher
Trying to open the scholarship form before completing the admission application (no application number, no scholarship form)
Letting the CGPA fall below 3.5 over 5.0 in any semester - performance is reviewed every semester and the award can be withdrawn
Quietly holding another scholarship, bursary or university loan without prior University approval
A weak 250-word essay, since it is the only free-text element and there is no choice of topic
Medicine or Renaissance Engineering Programme applicants waiting for the scholarship e-mail instead of checking with the school
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the S$6,500 yearly allowance; rent if you live off campus (the S$2,000 accommodation allowance applies only to NTU hostel residents); the non-subsidised portion of tuition if you decline the MOE Tuition Grant, which itself carries a three-year bond for Singapore PRs and international students; and any travel beyond the S$8,000 overseas-programme grant
document_audit: The referee must be a school teacher who is not a family member or relative, and needs your NTU application number and Date of Birth to submit
Only one online appraisal may be submitted to support the application
The essay is capped at 250 words on one compulsory topic - there is no choice of question
The passport-size photo must be a digital image uploaded as part of the process
The photo and appraisal deadlines are later than the scholarship deadline (26-28 March 2027 or 27 January 2027 depending on qualification) - completing the form alone is not enough
alerts: The 2027-round windows open 15 October 2026 (most international qualifications and IB) and 1 December 2026 (NUS High School) - the portals show 'closed' until then
Terminating the scholarship prematurely triggers a repayment obligation
No bond beyond the standard three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond for Singapore PRs and international students
The S$8,000 travel grant applies only to new cohorts from AY2025 and only to an overseas programme, under the Travel Grant Form terms
Student-ambassador duties (talks, receiving guests) are compulsory whenever the university calls
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first, then the scholarship form via the 'Apply for Scholarship' link with your NTU application number, essay and photo upload, teacher appraisal within 7 days, interview only if shortlisted in March-May, outcome by e-mail around mid-May

official.deadline_note: No NPGS application date is published: the official page states 'The application period for Academic Year 2027-2028 will be announced in due course' (the NIE application period is likewise to be announced). The related PhD admission deadlines for the August 2027 intake are 31 January 2027 generally, with school-specific earlier deadlines of 15 November 2026 (School of Art, Design and Media, School of Humanities, School of Social Sciences, Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information) and 31 December 2026 (LKCMedicine, S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies); the January intake opens 1 June and closes 31 July.
official.status_note: The official page states: 'The application period for Academic Year 2027-2028 will be announced in due course. The application period for National Institute of Education (NIE) will also be announced in due course.' The underlying PhD admission portal for the August 2027 intake opened on 1 October 2026, with the last day for submission of the online application and supporting documents on 31 January 2027 (earlier for some schools).
official.tuition_coverage_note: This award also covers the annual tuition fee.
benefits: Monthly stipend revised with effect from January 2026: S$5,300 (Singapore Citizen), S$4,800 (Singapore Permanent Resident), S$4,300 (International Student); the stipend remains the same for existing students receiving higher stipend rates
Coverage of the annual tuition fee
Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions at a rate pegged to the prevailing employer's contribution rate set by CPF, on top of the monthly stipend received, for Singapore Citizens
Overseas Conference Allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year (April previous year to March current year), revised with effect from April 2026
Book Allowance of S$500 per year; IT Allowance of S$1,500 (one-time); Thesis Allowance of S$600 (one-time, disbursed during the final year scholarship renewal)
Priority will be given for campus accommodation
eligibility: All nationalities are eligible for the scholarship
An Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level

Candidates who have not yet completed their undergraduate degree must provide official documentation from their university confirming they are on track to graduate with an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent
Outstanding graduates or final-year students taking their first step towards a leading research career by studying for a full-time PhD at NTU
requirements: Study for a full-time PhD at NTU and observe the terms and conditions for the award of the Scholarship

International Students must perform teaching/laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements of the Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP); Singaporeans and Singapore Permanent Residents may perform GAP at the discretion of the schools

New students must update their Singapore bank account details in the student intranet (GSLink) before the 15th of the semester commencement month (January or August) to avoid delays in stipend payment

The award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress; the maximum period is 4 years for PhD candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case
documents: Official documentation from the awarding university confirming the applicant is on track to graduate with an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent, if the undergraduate degree is not yet complete

PhD admission application documents submitted through the NTU graduate application portal: bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts (in English or with certified translation), a good TOEFL/IELTS score if the bachelor's degree is not conducted in English (valid within 2 years), two academic references, a research proposal (where applicable), a resume and a personal statement; GRE/GMAT/GATE optional and a video essay required for programmes under the College of Engineering and Interdisciplinary Graduate Programme
selection_criteria: Described by NTU as a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme - 'The premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognizing PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities'
Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level
Successful candidates are informed of the outcome together with the offer of admissions via email
Successful candidates are required to observe the terms and conditions for the award of the Scholarship
coverage: Monthly stipend of S$4,300 (International Student), S$4,800 (Singapore Permanent Resident) or S$5,300 (Singapore Citizen), revised with effect from January 2026
CPF contributions on top of the monthly stipend for Singapore Citizens
Overseas Conference Allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year (April previous year to March current year)
Book Allowance of S$500 annual grant; IT Allowance of S$1,500 one-time; Thesis Allowance of S$600 one-time
application_method: Apply for PhD admission at NTU through the graduate application portal (https://gradadmissions.ntu.edu.sg/apply) - for the August 2027 intake the portal opened 1 October 2026 and the last day for submission is 31 January 2027, with school-specific earlier deadlines
The NPGS application period for Academic Year 2027-2028 will be announced in due course; applicants interested in NIE programmes apply at the separate NIE intake portal

Successful candidates will be informed on the outcome of their application together with the offer of admissions via email and are required to observe the terms and conditions for the award of the Scholarship
official.application_route: Apply for full-time PhD admission through NTU's graduate application portal within the published intake window; the NPGS application period itself is announced separately by NTU and results arrive with the admission offer
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all nationalities; stipend tier is by citizenship - S$5,300 Singapore Citizen, S$4,800 Singapore Permanent Resident, S$4,300 International Student (revised with effect from January 2026). There is no bond attached to the scholarship
official.international_eligibility: All nationalities, including international students, are eligible. International Students receive the S$4,300 monthly rate and must perform teaching/laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements of the Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP)
official.research_requirement: Full-time PhD study at NTU based on independent but supervised research on an approved topic with a thesis submitted for examination; a research proposal is required as part of the admission application where applicable
official.duration: Tenable for one year in the first instance and renewable subject to good progress; the maximum period of the Scholarship is 4 years for PhD candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case
official.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship is NTU's competitive and prestigious flagship PhD scheme, designed to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying full-time for a PhD at NTU. As the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President it recognises PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities, and covers the annual tuition fee alongside a citizenship-tiered monthly stipend and conference, book, IT and thesis allowances.
official.program_type: Doctoral research scholarship - the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President
official.english_requirement: A good TOEFL/IELTS score for applicants whose Bachelor's degree is not conducted in English, with test scores valid within 2 years from the date of application; documents uploaded must be in English or accompanied by certified English translations. The scholarship page itself does not publish a separate English requirement.

not_confirmed: Exact NPGS application deadline for Academic Year 2027-2028 (the official page states it will be announced in due course)
Number of NPGS awards per cycle (not published)
verification.notes: Stipend tiers (revised January 2026), tuition-fee coverage, allowances, eligibility, duration, GAP condition and the 'announced in due course' status of the AY2027-2028 application period were read directly off NTU's NPGS page; the application route, intake windows, document list and English rule were cross-checked on NTU's Research Programmes Admission Guide. Both pages fetched 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: NTU's premier PhD award pays a citizenship-tiered monthly stipend - S$4,300 for international students, revised January 2026 - and covers the annual tuition fee, with conference, book, IT and thesis allowances on top, so awardees can concentrate on research rather than topping up funding. It is not a contest you can win in isolation: you apply for PhD admission, and the NPGS decision reaches you together with the offer of admission by e-mail. International awardees must plan for Graduate Assistantship Programme teaching or lab-supervision duties as part of the deal.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fresh graduates or final-year students with an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent bachelor's degree, of any nationality, who want a funded full-time PhD at NTU and can absorb teaching or supervision hours alongside research.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for PhD admission at https://gradadmissions.ntu.edu.sg/apply early - for the August 2027 intake the portal opened 1 October 2026 and closes 31 January 2027, but some schools close 15 November 2026
Request the official university letter confirming you are on track for an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree as soon as possible if your degree is not yet complete
Check whether your programme adds a video essay (College of Engineering and Interdisciplinary Graduate Programme) or requires GRE/GMAT/GATE
Line up two academic referees plus, where applicable, a research proposal, resume and personal statement in English or with certified translation
Watch the NPGS page for the AY2027-2028 application period announcement rather than assuming it tracks the admission dates
Once admitted, update your Singapore bank details in GSLink before the 15th of January or August so the first stipend and the automatic IT allowance are not delayed
common_rejection_risks: Falling below the published academic bar - Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level is stated up front
Missing your school's cut-off (15 November 2026 for ADM, SoH, SSS and WKWSCI; 31 December 2026 for LKCMedicine and RSIS) because you were watching the 31 January university-wide date
Treating the award as guaranteed for four years - it is tenable one year at a time and renewable only on good progress
Overlooking that International Students must perform Graduate Assistantship Programme teaching/laboratory supervision duties
Submitting supporting documents that are not in English or lack certified translations
Leaving stipend logistics to the last minute, so the first payment and the one-time IT allowance are delayed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The S$50 (nett) admission application fee; day-to-day living costs in Singapore beyond the fixed monthly stipend; and anything beyond the S$500 annual book allowance and the S$5,000 overseas conference allowance cap. Research funding availability can also cap the award period at less than four years
document_audit: If the bachelor's degree is incomplete, the on-track letter must come officially from your university - a supervisor's informal e-mail is not what the page describes
Every uploaded document must be in English or accompanied by a certified English translation
TOEFL/IELTS is only required if your bachelor's degree was not conducted in English, but the score must be within 2 years of application
A video essay is an extra mandatory item for College of Engineering and Interdisciplinary Graduate Programme applicants
International applicants need only a scanned passport, but Singapore Citizens/PRs must upload NRIC (and Re-Entry Permit for PRs)
alerts: The official page warns that scholarship coverage and award terms are subject to change and reserves the right to vary the stipend amount at any time
The stipend is tiered by citizenship, so the same award pays an international student S$1,000 a month less than a Singapore Citizen
The NPGS period for AY2027-2028 has not been announced yet ('will be announced in due course'), including for NIE
Exceeding the maximum PhD candidature period (5 years full-time) means paying fees at non-subsidised rates
No bond is attached, but the GAP teaching/supervision requirement effectively commits international awardees to service hours each year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online PhD admission application through NTU's graduate portal within your school's window; the NPGS outcome is communicated together with the offer of admissions by e-mail, with NIE applicants routed through a separate intake portal
